observations: body L1-L2: «Álbateniana» (L1) is printed with an acute over the A, 3.2 by 2.8 pt, a full accent like the acute over ǵ; the word has no accent elsewhere («Albateniana»); kept as printed. A speck after the t of «praebet» (L1) is not a stop; the e of «eius» (L1) is broken and prints like a c; a thin stroke 2 pt long hanging below the line before «arcus» (L2) is not a comma.

body L5: the formula treats the latitude β of the Moon and the difference in longitude Δλ as the legs of a right triangle, with sines for arcs: sin luminis : R = sin Δλ : √(sin² β + sin² Δλ). In the right spherical triangle with these legs the sine of the hypotenuse, the elongation, has sin² = sin² β + sin² Δλ − sin² β sin² Δλ; without the last term, the arc found is the angle of that triangle at the Moon, opposite Δλ, which is 90° when β = 0.

body L6-L13: «al–Khāzinī», «az–zīǵ», «as–sanǵarī» (L6), «87,r.–90,v.» (L7) and «al–Khuwārizmī» (L12) have long dashes (5.3 to 5.4 pt); the dashes before «Arcus» (L8), «Dicunt multi» (L10) and «Dicit Aḥmad» (L13) measure 10.1 to 10.4 pt, the dash before «Dicunt» on L11 7.1 pt, set as the same long rule. The limit of 12° for the arc of delay of the Indians and al-Khuwārizmī (L12-L13) is the 2 nāḍikā of p. 268, note 3: 48 minutes of time, in which 12° of the equator pass.

body L2-L3, L14-L20: «as–Sa‘īdī» (L15) has a long dash (about 5.5 pt, joined to the s), «al–Khāzinī» (L20) one of 5.3 pt; the dashes before «Dicit Kūshiyār» (L16) and «In III capite» (L20) measure 9.8 and 10.1 pt. Ḥabash's limit of 10° for the depression of the Sun (L14) is the one stated on L2-L3; as-Sa‘īdī reports 8° 2/3 after him (L15). Kūshiyār's sum of 18° (L19) is his arc of light, 10°, and his arc of depression, 8° (L17-L18).

body L21-L25: «87,v.–88,r.» and «88,r.–89,r.» (L21) have long dashes (5.3 pt); a speck about 1 pt across at the foot after the semicolon of «88,r.);» (L21) is not a stop. «al-Battānī» (L22, L23) is letter-spaced, with hyphens (3.5 and 3.4 pt); the dashes before «Inter» (L22) and «Prior» (L24) measure 9.2 and 9.4 pt. «قوَمنا» (L25) is printed with a fatha over the wāw, a slanted stroke 2.5 pt long, and no shadda; the verb is qawwamnā, "we have computed the true places"; kept as printed.

body L26-L34: al-Khāzinī's 12° 1/6 (L27), written 12° 10′ on L28, L30 and L34, stands for al-Battānī's 12° 11′ (p. 268, rule II); the mean arc of visibility of 11° 45′ (L28-L29) is al-Battānī's (p. 267). «al–Battānī» (L31) is letter-spaced, with a long dash (5.5 pt).

notes_left L1-L4: note 1 gives the Arabic of the title of chapter II and of the sentence that L7-L10 of the text translate. The dash before «Ex» (L4) measures 7.4 pt; «87,v.-88,r.» (L4) has a hyphen (3.2 pt).
notes_left L7: «altitudi» has no printed hyphen at the end of the line; kept as printed.

notes_right L1-L5: the dash before «Hoc» (L1) measures 8.0 pt. The reading of the codex, «السعدى» (L3), as-Sa‘dī, is printed with the teeth of the sīn as low bumps on a drawn-out stroke; the name that Suter proposed, as-Sa‘īdī (L5), has a yā’ before the dāl. The hyphen of «al-Ḥāzimī» is printed at the end of L4 (3.5 pt) and again, as a long dash (4.4 pt), at the beginning of L5; «as-Sa‘īdī» (L5) has a hyphen (3.0 pt).
notes_right L8-L9: «p» before «83–» (L8) is printed without its stop; kept as printed. «83–» ends L8 with a long dash (5.2 pt) and «-84» begins L9 with a hyphen (3.2 pt).
